image_description: A close-up, low-angle view of a modern staircase featuring a metal bannister system. The handrail is a sleek, tubular metal bar running diagonally upwards. It is supported by thin, vertical metal balusters (rods) that are evenly spaced. To the left, there is a darker wooden structure or secondary railing element. The steps appear to be made of light-colored stone or concrete with visible treads. The lighting is cool and slightly dim, casting shadows between the balusters.

The texture on the stair treads is slightly smeared and lacks the fine grain expected of stone or concrete. There is a slight 'waxy' sheen on the metal that doesn't fully match realistic specular highlights.
The background railing/grid pattern becomes slightly inconsistent in perspective density, appearing to warp slightly rather than maintaining strict linear perspective convergence.
